text: The Denali Park Road has been closed at Mile 43 (East Fork Bridge) since 2021 due to the Pretty Rocks Landslide. NPS has targeted full bus service to Eielson/Wonder Lake/Kantishna to resume in 2027, but hasn't confirmed a date — the plan is built around the Mile 43 turnaround as the safe assumption. Worth reconfirming on the NPS Denali "current conditions" page closer to your travel date; if the full road has reopened by then, a longer bus ride becomes possible but likely wouldn't fit in the same day as the drive to Fairbanks.

images.credit: Photo by Tim Rains / NPS, public domain
images.caption: Denali National Park tundra landscape

text: Coldfoot Camp Cafe runs buffet-only service in summer — breakfast buffet 5–9am, dinner buffet 5–9pm. Between those windows, only truckers can order off the menu, so the plan eats lunch on the road rather than at Coldfoot.

images.credit: Photo by Scott McMurren / CC BY 2.0
images.caption: Coldfoot Camp, the world's northernmost truck stop

text: As currently built, Gates of the Arctic gets exactly two attempts before you're committed to driving south. Two consecutive bad-weather days at Coldfoot would mean missing the park outright, with no later point in the trip to circle back. Worth deciding whether to add a third buffer day at Coldfoot (pulled from the Lake Clark/Katmai reserve, currently at 5 days).

images.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain
images.caption: Aerial view of the Brooks Range, Gates of the Arctic

text: This fits both Kennecott essentials into 2 days and satisfies the lodge's 2-night minimum. It does mean skipping the dedicated Wrangell–St. Elias flightseeing day — worth reconsidering during the buffer pass, either as an early-morning add-on before the Root Glacier hike on July 4, or reinstated as a third day if you'd rather not compress further.

images.credit: Photo by Michael F. Wacht / CC BY-SA 4.0
images.caption: The historic Kennecott copper concentration mill

text: Taking the early flight turns this from a pure travel day into a bonus buffer day for Kobuk Valley — you land with the afternoon still open instead of arriving in the evening.

images.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain
images.caption: Aerial view of Kotzebue on the Chukchi Sea coast

text: Operators: K2 Aviation, Talkeetna Air Taxi, or Sheldon Air Service, all out of Talkeetna Airport (TKA).

images.credit: Photo by Jacob W. Frank / NPS, CC BY 2.0
images.caption: Flightseeing plane wing over Denali and the Alaska Range

text: Optional, book ahead: Mount Wrangell flightseeing with Copper Valley Air Service — no walk-in hours; "Three Peak Tour" (~60 min, ~$400/person, Mt. Sanford/Mt. Drum/Mt. Wrangell) or "Flight of Majesty" (~120 min, adds mud volcanoes and wildlife) — would replace one of the day's other stops given the long drive.

images.credit: Photo by B. Cella / NPS, public domain
images.caption: Mount Wrangell shield volcano seen from the southwest

text: If Gates of the Arctic still doesn't happen after both attempts, there's no ground alternative to fall back on — unlike Denali or Wrangell–St. Elias, this park is fly-in only, so missing it means missing the park entirely.

images.credit: Photo by Paxson Woelber / Expedition Arguk, CC BY 2.0
images.caption: Drizzly, low-cloud day in the Central Brooks Range

text: Flights to Anchorage from Florida: MIA, FLL, TPA, MCO, RSW.

images.credit: Photo by Wonderlane / CC BY 2.0
images.caption: Main lobby of the South Terminal, Ted Stevens Airport

text: No dedicated weather buffer day for this flight — per the note that missing one flightseeing tour among many isn't a big loss.

images.credit: Photo by Jacob W. Frank / NPS, CC BY 2.0
images.caption: Flightseeing plane wing over Denali and the Alaska Range

text: Jul 1 is a dual-purpose day: if Jun 30's flight was weathered out, this is the backup attempt (still flying during the day and driving back to Fairbanks that same night); otherwise it's just the drive-back day.

images.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain
images.caption: Aerial view of the Brooks Range, Gates of the Arctic

text: Copper Valley Air Service (Gulkana Airport, Glennallen, ~15 min from Copper Center): "Three Peak Tour" (~60 min, ~$400/person, fly-over of Mt. Sanford, Mt. Drum, Mt. Wrangell, no landing) or "Flight of Majesty" (~120 min, adds mud volcanoes and wildlife spotting). Weather-dependent, but optional and slotted into a non-dedicated day, so no schedule impact if skipped.

images.credit: Photo by B. Cella / NPS, public domain
images.caption: Mount Wrangell shield volcano seen from the southwest

text: Kennicott Glacier Lodge has a 2-night minimum and very limited dining alternatives on-site (their dining room, the Meatza Wagon food truck, or a trip into McCarthy) — a meal package is worth booking.

images.credit: Courtesy of Kennicott Glacier Lodge
images.caption: Kennicott Glacier Lodge near the historic copper mill

text: Kotzebue has no direct flights from Fairbanks — all routes connect through Anchorage. The Kennecott → Anchorage drive happens July 5 (with the Matanuska Glacier stop), and the Jul 6 outbound flight is the early one (~8:40–9am, landing ~10:30am) rather than an afternoon flight — this opens a same-day bonus attempt at Kobuk Valley on top of Jul 7 and Jul 8, giving three possible flying days instead of two. Jul 9 remains a flex morning + late flight back.

images.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain
images.caption: Aerial view of Kotzebue on the Chukchi Sea coast

text: Lake Clark/Katmai structure (Port Alsworth stay vs. Anchorage day trips) is still open — once decided, activities/hotel/restaurant will be filled in the same way as the rest of the trip.

images.credit: Photo by Richard A. Weaver / CC BY-SA 4.0
images.caption: Brown bear fishing for salmon at Brooks Falls

text: The Whittier tunnel (Anton Anderson Memorial Tunnel) runs one-lane alternating traffic on a schedule, not free-flow — worth checking timing before the drive down so you're not stuck waiting right before boarding.

images.credit: Photo by Gabor Eszes / CC BY-SA 3.0
images.caption: West portal of the Anton Anderson Memorial Tunnel

text: Cruise Itinerary — port order, arrival/departure times may vary by sailing date; confirm final schedule closer to departure. The two dedicated glacier-viewing days (Hubbard + Glacier Bay) give natural redundancy if weather affects one of them.

images.credit: Photo by Blake Handley / CC BY 2.0
images.caption: Discovery Princess docked at Ogden Point, Victoria BC

text: Kennecott was compressed from 3 nights to 2 (Root Glacier hike + Mill Tour fit into one full day), which originally freed up July 5 — now used for the Matanuska Glacier helicopter tour en route to Anchorage. The dedicated Wrangell–St. Elias flightseeing day is still the one dropped in this compression; still worth reconsidering during the buffer re-evaluation pass if you'd rather not have skipped it.

images.credit: Photo by Michael F. Wacht / CC BY-SA 4.0

text: Deposit of $198.00 paid Aug 6, 2026 (100% non-refundable, per Princess's deposit terms). Remaining balance of $9,138.00 (total fare $9,336.00 for all four passengers, less the deposit) is due by Apr 18, 2027.

text: Cancellation fees escalate fast after final payment: 25% of total charges from Apr 19, 2027, 50% from May 4, 75% from May 18, and 100% (no refund) from Jun 17, 2027 through sailing — worth locking in the parks-leg plan well before mid-April, since backing out of the cruise gets expensive quickly after that.
